summary.intent: Update the release-notes redesign artifact with an architecture section, then start steps 1 and 2 of the plan: introduce a serializable, versioned ReleaseNotes model and refactor the release PR body renderer to build from it.
summary.outcome: Added release_notes.rs in callisto-graph, refactored commands/pr_body.rs to use it with rendered output unchanged, updated versioning docs, and ran fmt, clippy and tests. Committed and pushed to feat/release-notes-model, then began checking the `entire trail` CLI to create the trail and link the branch before any PR.

repo: The callisto-graph crate holds the release PR body logic (commands/pr_body.rs) and now a new release_notes.rs module registered in lib.rs.
Lint gate is `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph -p callisto-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, so unused imports break it and must be fixed rather than ignored.
Subprocess dispatch behavior is covered by the callisto-cli test `subprocess_dispatch_and_stdin_tests`, which was run as a regression check for the refactor.
Architecture documentation for versioning lives in docs/architecture/versioning.md and was updated alongside the code change.
Work is done in a git worktree at .claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners, while the pushed branch is feat/release-notes-model, so worktree name and branch name differ.
Git is invoked as /usr/bin/git with commit.gpgsign=false for non-interactive commits.

code.finding: `assess` was only used by the test-only wrapper after the refactor, so its import was moved into the test scope to satisfy clippy.

workflow: Helper scripts (add_arch.py, splice.py) are written to a separate jobs tmp dir and run with `python3 -I`, keeping them apart from the files they edit.
A refactor was validated in order: cargo fmt, clippy with -D warnings, unit tests, then a CLI integration test, before committing.
The user asked for the trail to be created and the branch linked before opening any PR, so the `entire trail` CLI is used for that step.

friction: Clippy flagged an unused `assess` import after the refactor, requiring a second fmt/clippy/test pass.
Test code was appended to release_notes.rs via a shell heredoc-style redirect from a temp file, then needed a tail, grep and wc check plus a follow-up edit to confirm placement, which was fiddly.
The commit and push were chained in one command with only the last line of push output shown, so a push failure could be easy to miss.
open_items: Create the entire trail and link feat/release-notes-model to it before opening a PR; the `entire trail --help` check was only just started.
Open the PR for the ReleaseNotes model refactor after the trail is linked.
Later steps of the release-notes redesign plan beyond steps 1 and 2 remain.
Confirm the push to origin succeeded, since only the tail of its output was captured.
